text:
alex: customer hit a 400 on function call when passing an XML payload inside the tool args. they pasted an xml attribute with single quotes and our parser chose the wrong tool :/

miriam: can you paste the exact arg string? is it coming from a client copy/paste or generated server-side?

alex: pasted from a legacy system. here's the field that trips it (redacted):

alex: ```json
{
  "target_tool": "extract-metadata",
  "payload": "<file name='report.pdf' author='‘JDoe’' size=\"42KB\">...</file>"
}
```

samir: aha — note those curly single quotes around JDoe (U+2018/U+2019) and the mix of single and double quotes inside the XML attribute. our client-side preprocessor tries to normalize quotes and ends up unbalancing the JSON string, which makes the router fallback to the generic text-tool instead of `extract-metadata`.

ingrid: log excerpt from the invocation: `parsed_args.tool_name=null, selected_tool=text-analyzer` and we return 400 with body `invalid tool arguments` (schema validation fail).

alex: reproduced locally by pasting that line into the web app. steps: 1) paste xml snippet into argument input, 2) click run tool, 3) observe 400 and tool selection mismatch.

miriam: severity? customer blocked?

alex: P1 for them — automated invoice ingestion is broken. They can work around by replacing curly quotes with straight ones, but it's manual and not acceptable long-term.

samir: quick triage: root cause is our naive JSON-string sanitizer in the browser that replaces smart quotes with straight quotes but doesn't escape inner quotes in XML attributes. On roundtrip the string becomes malformed, sending something like: `{"target_tool":"extract-metadata","payload":"<file name=\"report.pdf\" author=\"JDoe\" ...>"}` vs expected properly escaped string.

ingrid: proposed short-term mitigation: server-side tolerant parser — accept `payload` as raw string even if inner quotes aren't escaped, then attempt to detect intended `target_tool` from heuristics. Will open a guarded fallback that only applies to enterprise tenants with this flag.

miriam: can you attach a minimal repro request that support can forward to the customer? they want scriptable steps.

alex: yes — curl payload below (sanitized account ids):

alex: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"target_tool":"extract-metadata","payload":"<file name='report.pdf' author=‘JDoe’>"}'
```

samir: thanks. I pushed a quick dev-only fix to the client sanitizer to prefer escaping inner double-quotes and normalizing curly quotes to straight ascii before sending. will open PR and flag eng-runtime for review if server fallback is needed.

ingrid: logging request ids? we need the customer request-id to find server logs. alex can you DM the customer and grab `x-request-id` from their failing attempts?

alex: requested, they sent back `x-request-id: rq_0ab12cd34ef`. forwarded to samir.

support-bot: escalation created: INC-2026 linked to this thread, assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml for tool-routing heuristics.

samir: plan: (1) hotfix client sanitizer and deploy to web app (low risk) — ETA 6h, (2) implement server tolerant-fallback for target_tool detection behind an enterprise flag — ETA 3d, (3) add unit tests & corpus cases for smart quotes, BOM, and mixed-quote XML fragments — ETA 5d.

miriam: add a KB note for support with the curl snippet and the simple workaround (replace curly quotes or wrap payload in base64). also mention to set enterprise flag if we enable fallback.

alex: customer accepted base64 workaround as a temporary step. I'll keep thread updated when they confirm ingestion. :thumbsup:

ingrid: tagging @oncall for visibility. if errors spike after client rollout, escalate to infra.

samir: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/webapp/pull/872 (dev-only sanitizer). requesting quick review.

alex: thanks team — keeping this thread updated with customer confirmations and any regressions.
